title: Frozen Tissue Nuclei Extraction
author: Carly Martin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbseinbe
materials: Make dissociation buffer , 50 mLs per sample:
Chill all buffers to 4C , and keep all buffers on ice when in use.

Prepare equipment: Set out and chill the following equipment/supplies. The instructions below are for one sample. ● Cold block dissecting tray, kept at -20C ● Chill clean razor blades and glass slides on the cold dissecting tray ● Chill 3 mL syringe with 26 1⁄2 gauge needle, at 4C, one syringe and needle per sample ● Place a 12-well tissue-culture plate, well-bottoms colored with marker, on ice * Color the underside of the culture plate with dark marker so you can see your sample dissociate ● Place 2 mL chilled extraction buffer in the first well of 12-well plate ● Place ~50 mL chilled DB in a falcon tube on ice ● Locate DAPI (1:1000) (https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/D1306) ● Locate a 100um filter for falcon tubes, place in 4C (https://us.vwr.com/store/product/14796270/vwr-cell-strainers-dnase-rnase-free-non-pyrogenic-sterile) ● Locate 50 μm eppendorf tube filter, place in 4C (https://us.sysmex-flowcytometry.com/consumables/celltrics-filters/sterile-single-p ack-celltrics filters/1445/sterile-single-pack-celltrics-filters-50/box?number=04-00 4-2327) ● Place 2 50 mL tubes on ice ● Locate a c-Chip FR hemocytometer

Locate supplies for FACS: ● 96 well cold block, chilled to -20C: (https://www.daigger.com/eppendorf-pcr-coolers-14616-group?gclid=EAIaIQobCh MI2rKM7aDN4AIVDRgMCh2jkwRMEAQYBSABEgKeA_D_BwE) ● 200uL 5% BSA-DB ● 20uL collection buffer: DB with 1:40 RNAse-inhibitor * Prepare the collection buffer right before beginning FACS session

Begin extraction. Perform all steps with cold buffers on ice. Nuclei should never leave the ice or 4C environment. Chop up tissue on the chilled dissection tray. If your sample is a very small piece (less than 3mm in any dimension) you can forgo this step and place sample immediately into the extraction buffer. Place the frozen sample on the glass slide and shave the frosty/freezer-burned tissue face you want to sample from off the sample and discard. This is damaged and not worth extracting. Then, moving rapidly but carefully, shave off “enough” sample to work with. Rapidly mince the shaved sample with the 2 chilled razor blades that were used to shave the tissue block and scrape into the first well of a 6-well plate that contains 2 mL of cold extraction buffer. Pipette up and down 20 times.

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Make 3 mL extraction buffer per sample containing Dissociation Buffer, 1 % Kollidon VA64, 1 % Triton X‑100, and RNase‑inhibitor at a 1:40 dilution.

steps.title: Incubate with detergent
steps.instruction: Incubate samples in the extraction buffer for 10 min, pipetting up and down 20 times (≈every 2.5 min) with a 1000 µL pipette set to 1000 µL.

steps.title: Mechanical dissociation
steps.instruction: Pull the sample into a chilled needle/syringe and expel back into the same well for final dissociation; repeat if large chunks remain.

steps.title: Large‑volume wash
steps.instruction: Transfer nuclei to an empty 30 mL tube and add chilled DB until the total volume is just under 30 mL.

steps.title: Split nuclei suspension
steps.instruction: Aliquot the diluted nuclei into two 50 mL conical tubes, ~15 mL per tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes at 600 rcf in a swinging‑bucket centrifuge for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Aspirate ~13 mL wash buffer with a serological pipette, then gently aspirate the remaining supernatant with a P1000 pipette, leaving 300–500 µL. Resuspend nuclei by pipetting without creating bubbles and pool the paired samples.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate remaining supernatant with P1000, leave 300‑500 µL

steps.title: Filter nuclei clumps
steps.instruction: Wet a 40 µm Eppendorf filter tip with cold DB, then pass ~0.5–1 mL of the washed sample through the filter into an epi tube.

steps.title: Stain nuclei with DAPI
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL DAPI to 1 mL nuclei suspension, mix, then remove 20 µL and load into a Fast‑Read hemocytometer for concentration and quality assessment.

steps.title: Prepare PCR tubes for FACS
steps.instruction: Fill each PCR tube with 5 % BSA‑DB, vortex, discard the BSA solution, wash with 200 µL DB, then add 20 µL collection buffer (DB with 1:40 RNase‑inhibitor). Keep tubes on a –20 °C 96‑well block.

steps.title: FACS singlet enrichment
steps.instruction: Run samples on a Sony SH800 sorter using a 70 µm chip, set a 1 % FSC threshold on the DAPI singlet peak, and collect sorted nuclei into the prepared PCR tubes.

steps.title: Determine nuclei concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the volume in each PCR tube, make a 1:10 dilution by mixing 2 µL nuclei with 18 µL chilled DB, load into a Fast‑Read hemocytometer, count all 16 large squares, average the count, then multiply by 10 and by 5 (hemocytometer factor) to obtain nuclei / µL.

steps.title: Prepare for 10X sequencing
steps.instruction: Use up to 17 000 nuclei (≈10 000 after loss); for 10x v3 the input volume is 46.6 µL, corresponding to a maximum concentration of 364 nuclei/µL.
